span.label: mechanisms
span.term: statistical laws of semantic change: the rate of change scales as an inverse power-law of word frequency (law of conformity) and rises with polysemy (law of innovation)
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper's results are correlational; it explicitly declines to claim the causal mechanisms it speculates about.
span.note: what this limits: the mechanistic story: WHILE OUR RESULTS CANNOT CONFIRM SUCH CAUSAL LINKS, THEY NONETHELESS HIGHLIGHT A NEW ROLE FOR FREQUENCY AND POLYSEMY - correlational by the authors' own statement
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The polysemy proxy (local clustering coefficient in a PPMI co-occurrence network) is biased towards rating contextually diverse function words as highly polysemous.
span.note: what this limits: every polysemy score: the measure IS SLIGHTLY BIASED TOWARDS RATING CONTEXTUALLY DIVERSE DISCOURSE FUNCTION WORDS (E.G., ALSO) AS HIGHLY POLYSEMOUS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Polysemy has no agreed ground truth to validate the measure against.
span.note: what this limits: any validation of a polysemy measure at all: MEASURING WORD POLYSEMY IS A DIFFICULT AND FRAUGHT TASK, AS EVEN 'GROUND TRUTH' DICTIONARIES DIFFER IN THE NUMBER OF SENSES THEY ASSIGN TO WORDS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The main corpora contain artifacts from shifting sampling biases over time.
span.note: what this limits: every result computed on that corpus: THE GOOGLE N-GRAM DATASETS ... CONTAIN MANY CORPUS ARTIFACTS DUE, E.G., TO SHIFTING SAMPLING BIASES OVER TIME
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Part of the polysemy result (the negative curvature at high polysemy) is not robust across datasets or methods.
span.note: what this limits: the polysemy curvature result specifically: IT VARIES ACROSS DATASETS AND WAS NOT PRESENT WITH SGNS, SO IT IS NOT AS ROBUST AS THE CLEAR LINEAR TREND
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper's second law is stated in two logically different forms, two pages apart.
span.note: what this limits: any citation of the law of innovation: the abstract states it as holding independent of frequency, while the introduction states it as holding after controlling for frequency and adds 'significantly', and the two are not the same claim
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: One of the three methods is stated to be prone to false discoveries.
span.note: what this limits: any result computed with PPMI embeddings: the authors state it performs poorly on all the benchmark tasks, is extremely sensitive to rare events, and is prone to false discoveries from global genre shifts
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The choice between the two remaining methods is left unsettled by the paper's own benchmarks.
span.note: what this limits: any rate of semantic change quoted from this work: between SVD and SGNS the results are described as somewhat equivocal, with each performing best on two of the four tasks
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the law of innovation - TWO STATEMENTS, ONE NAME: the abstract has it holding 'independent of frequency' and the introduction 'after controlling for frequency', with 'significantly' added in the second; independence and a residual surviving adjustment are different claims, and the name that travels does not say which one is meant
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a rate of semantic change - A NUMBER PRODUCED BY A CHOICE OF EMBEDDING: PPMI, SVD and SGNS are ranked against each other by the paper itself, PPMI is called clearly worse and prone to false discoveries from genre shifts, and between the other two the result is equivocal - so the construct's value depends on an instrument the paper declines to settle
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a law - PROPOSED, NOT DERIVED: the authors say they PROPOSE two statistical laws relating frequency and polysemy to semantic change, fitted over six corpora, and the record's existing limitation already records that the analysis is correlational and the causal mechanisms are declined
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Using diachronic word embeddings (word2vec/PPMI/SVD) over six corpora, four languages, two centuries, two statistical laws of semantic change emerge: (i) law of conformity — change rate scales with an inverse power-law of word frequency; (ii) law of innovation — more polysemous words change faster, independent of frequency.
